_notes: Desired Bitbucket Cloud branch restrictions for the EDW Flyway repository. Applied by
bitbucket/apply_branch_restrictions.sh: it creates missing kinds, updates changed ones and never deletes.
Keys starting with '_' are documentation and are never sent to Bitbucket.
'groups_env' names an environment variable holding comma-separated Bitbucket group slugs; the script turns
it into the API's 'groups' list. Only 'push' and 'restrict_merges' accept users/groups, and an EMPTY list
Kinds and value semantics: the branchrestriction schema in api.bitbucket.org/swagger.json (read 2026-10-13).
Plan caveats (verify on the workspace): enforce_merge_checks ('Prevent a merge with unresolved merge
checks') is believed to need Bitbucket Premium; on Free/Standard the merge checks are advisory and the hard
gate is Jenkins (MGM/PRD deploy jobs only take bundles built from main).
Default reviewers are individual users (the API has no group form): add them at project or repository
level, or require_default_reviewer_approvals_to_merge can never be met.

_why: No direct pushes to main: every change arrives through a reviewed, Jenkins-validated pull request.
Only the optional break-glass group may push (unset = nobody), for a recorded emergency.
Only the EDW merge group may press Merge.
Required: an empty list here would block every merge, so the script refuses to send one.
No force-push: rewriting main orphans migrations already applied on a runway (guard FG003).
At least one of those approvals comes from a default reviewer (DBA / data architect).
The Jenkins PR build (guard, Flyway code review, info + validate against DEV) must be green.
An open 'request changes' blocks the merge.
Open pull request tasks (review to-dos) block the merge.
A new push to the source branch withdraws earlier approvals: reviewers approve what merges.
Makes the checks above blocking instead of advisory. Believed Premium-only (verify); on a plan that
refuses it, run the script with --skip enforce_merge_checks.
